mainTopic: An owner redeeming his consecrated field in the second יובל, and a field a son bought from his father
overview: The גמרא asks whether, according to רבי אליעזר, an owner who redeems his consecrated ancestral field only in the second יובל cycle counts as 'another person' (כאחר). It first tries a proof from a ברייתא on the word ״עוד״. That proof falls away when the גמרא shows the ברייתא can be read as a field a כהן consecrated, a reading that works for every תנא. The גמרא then explains why the Torah needed ״לא יגאל״, ״לאשר קנהו״ and ״עוד״. Next it brings a ברייתא of רבי אליעזר, which comes in two versions: in one, the owner in the second יובל is like another person and the field goes to the כהנים; in the other, he is not, and he keeps it. A new משנה follows about a son who buys a field from his father: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון disagree on whether it is a שדה אחוזה or a שדה מקנה. The משנה also teaches that a שדה מקנה never goes to the כהנים, and that כהנים and לוים may always consecrate and redeem. The גמרא suggests their argument depends on whether קנין פירות is like קנין הגוף. רב נחמן בר יצחק begins to answer, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Is the owner treated like a stranger in the second Jubilee cycle?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a dilemma: if the owner redeems his consecrated field during the second יובל cycle, is he like another person or not?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: if the owner redeems his field in the second יובל cycle, is he treated like an outsider or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about an owner who redeems his consecrated field late, in the second יובל cycle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, if the owner redeems before the first יובל, the field stays his forever. If an outsider redeems it, it goes to the כהנים at יובל. The question is which group a late-redeeming owner falls into.

keyTerms.meaning: A dilemma, an open question
The owner of the field
The Jubilee year, every 50 years
He is considered like another person

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
The owner, in the second Jubilee cycle,
phrases.notes: He means an owner who consecrated his ancestral field and only redeemed it after the first יובל passed.

phrases.english: is he considered like another person, or not?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a late-redeeming owner (second יובל) is treated like an outsider, so the field goes to the כהנים at the next יובל.

steps.title: A teaching on the word 'anymore'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: the owner cannot redeem the field to be as it was, but can redeem it as a purchased field.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: ״It shall not be redeemed״. You might think it can't be redeemed at all, not even as a purchased field. The verse says ״anymore״: it can't be redeemed to go back to how it was, but it can be redeemed as a purchased field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that may answer the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads ״עוד״ as limiting the rule. The owner loses the field's status as a permanent ancestral field, but he can still buy it back as a שדה מקנה, which he does not keep for good at יובל. That is like how an outsider who redeems is treated.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought
A purchased field (not inherited)
The verse teaches
Anymore; read here as a limit on the rule

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"It shall not be redeemed" —
one might think it shall not be redeemed at all,
not even to be his like a purchased field?
The verse teaches "anymore" —
to be as it was, it is not redeemed,
but it is redeemed
to be his like a purchased field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the dilemma
steps.raayaObject: That the owner is like an outsider in the second יובל

steps.title: Which Jubilee cycle is the teaching talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when the ברייתא applies. It can't mean the first יובל, because then the field is still fully ancestral. So it must mean the second יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: When? If you say in the first יובל, why can't he get it back as it was? It is still an ancestral field then! Rather, it obviously means the second יובל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pins down the time the ברייתא is speaking about, to connect it to our question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the first יובל, an owner who redeems gets his ancestral field back fully. So the ברייתא's rule, 'only as a purchased field', can't be about that time. It must be about the second יובל, which is exactly our case.

keyTerms.meaning: When?
If you say
Ancestral field, inherited land
It is obvious

phrases.english: When?
If you say during the first Jubilee cycle —
why can it not be redeemed as it was?
It is also still an ancestral field!
Rather, it is obvious: during the second Jubilee cycle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the time frame of the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which יובל cycle the ברייתא refers to
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second יובל cycle, since in the first the owner gets back a full אחוזה

steps.title: Whose opinion is the teaching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view the ברייתא follows. It can't be רבי יהודה or רבי שמעון, because for them the field already went to the כהנים at the first יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to whom? If רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, the field already goes out to the כהנים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks which תנא could hold this ברייתא and rules out two of them. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, an unredeemed field goes to the כהנים at the first יובל. So in the second cycle there is nothing left to redeem at all, and the ברייתא can't follow them.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to whom?
Priests
It goes out, passes to

phrases.english: And according to whom?
If according to Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon —
it already goes out to the priests!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן? אִי לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After fixing the time, identifies the author of the ברייתא

steps.title: The teaching follows רבי אליעזר, so the owner is like a stranger
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא must follow רבי אליעזר, so we learn that an owner redeeming in the second יובל is like another person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it must be רבי אליעזר. Learn from this: the owner in the second יובל is considered like another person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof and seems to answer the original dilemma. The next step challenges this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר the field stays with הקדש until someone redeems it, so redemption in the second cycle is possible. Since the ברייתא says the owner gets it only as a purchased field, he is treated like an outsider.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not
Learn from it; a conclusion

steps.whatToRemember: This proof looks like it settles the question: according to רבי אליעזר, an owner who redeems in the second יובל is כאחר. But step 6 attacks it, step 7 re-reads the ברייתא, and the proof falls away.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not according to Rabbi Eliezer?
And learn from it:
the owner in the second Jubilee cycle is considered like another person.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies רבי אליעזר as the author and resolves the dilemma
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי אליעזר, an owner in the second יובל is like an outsider.

steps.title: What do רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון learn from the word עוד?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges its own conclusion. If the ברייתא only fits רבי אליעזר, then what do רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון learn from the word עוד?
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really explain it that way?! If so, what do רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון learn from the word 'anymore' (עוד)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the conclusion it just reached, that the ברייתא follows only רבי אליעזר. It asks what the other תנאים do with the word עוד in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in the Torah teaches something to every תנא. If the ברייתא's teaching from עוד only works for רבי אליעזר, then רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון are left with a word that teaches nothing. That means there must be a reading of the ברייתא that works for them too.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you really understand it that way? A word that signals the גמרא doubts the previous explanation
'Anymore' – the word in the פסוק 'לא יגאל עוד' that the ברייתא learns from
They learn from it (by explaining the פסוק)

phrases.english: And can you really understand it that way?!
Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon:
what do they learn from this word "anymore"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion of step 5 that the ברייתא follows only רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר alone.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון must also learn something from עוד, so the ברייתא should be readable for them as well.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about a field a כהן consecrated
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the ברייתא as a new case: the field already went to the כהנים, a כהן consecrated it, and the original owner came to redeem it. עוד teaches that he can redeem it only as a purchased field.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what case are we dealing with? A field that already went to the כהנים, and a כהן consecrated it, and then the original owner came to redeem it. You might have thought he cannot redeem it at all, not even as a purchased field. So the פסוק says עוד: he cannot redeem it back to how it was (as his ancestral field), but he can redeem it so that for him it is like a purchased field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new reading of the ברייתא that works even for רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון. It is about a field that already went to the כהנים and was then consecrated by a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the original owner lost his field to the כהנים at the first יובל, so everyone agrees it is no longer his ancestral field. The word עוד teaches that he can still redeem it, but only with the status of a שדה מקנה, not as his own inheritance. Because of this new reading, the ברייתא no longer proves anything about the question from step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? Used to give a new reading of a source
A consecrated field that was not redeemed and went to the כהנים at יובל
A purchased field, not inherited family land
You might have thought (a mistaken first idea)
Therefore the פסוק says, to teach otherwise

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the earlier reading. Before, the ברייתא was about the owner redeeming in the second יובל. Now it is about a field the כהן himself consecrated after it already became his.
steps.whyThisMatters: This reading removes the proof for the dilemma from step 1. The גמרא comes back to that question in step 13.

phrases.english: Rather, what case are we dealing with here?
With a field that went out to the priests,
and a priest consecrated it,
and the original owners came to redeem it.
You might have thought:
it may not be redeemed,
even to be like a purchased field.
So the verse says: "anymore":
it may not be redeemed to be as it was,
phrases.notes: "As it was" means as his own family land.

phrases.english: but it may be redeemed
so that for him it is like a purchased field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 by placing the ברייתא in a case that works for all תנאים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about the owner redeeming in the second יובל, and it follows only רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a field a כהן consecrated after it went to the כהנים; the owner may redeem it only as a שדה מקנה.

steps.title: Support: the field does not return to the treasurer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. The פסוק 'the field shall return to the one from whom it was bought' does not mean the הקדש treasurer. It means the one who owns the land as an inheritance.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so it is taught in a ברייתא: 'The field shall return to the one from whom it was bought.' You might think it goes back to the גזבר from whom he bought it when he redeemed it. So the פסוק says: 'to the one to whom the possession of the land belongs,' the owner of the family land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports its new reading. This ברייתא begins by explaining who gets the field back at יובל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who redeems a purchased field from הקדש technically 'bought' it from the גזבר. The ברייתא rules out the idea that the field goes back to the גזבר; it goes to the one whose inherited land it is. This sets up the next question: then what does 'לאשר קנהו' teach?

keyTerms.meaning: The treasurer of הקדש, who handles its property
Inherited family land
One might think (a possible but wrong idea)

phrases.english: And so it is taught:
"The field shall return
to the one from whom it was bought,"
one might think it returns to the treasurer
from whom he took it?
So the verse says:
"to the one to whom the possession of the land belongs."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a supporting ברייתא for the reading in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that a field that went to the כהנים is treated as the כהן's own.

steps.title: The field goes back to the כהן who sold it
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains 'לאשר קנהו': the field went to the כהנים, a כהן sold it, the buyer consecrated it, and someone else redeemed it. At יובל it goes back to the כהן, not to the original owners.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then why does the פסוק say 'to the one from whom it was bought'? It is about a field that went to the כהנים, and the כהן sold it, and the buyer consecrated it, and someone else redeemed it. You might think it goes back to the original owners. So the פסוק says 'to the one from whom it was bought,' meaning the כהן who sold it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and explains the extra phrase in the פסוק. It teaches that once a field went to the כהנים, the כהן is now the one it returns to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the reading in step 7. Once the field went to the כהנים, the original owner's family rights are gone and the כהן has taken his place. So whether the כהן consecrates it himself or sells it to someone else, the original owner does not get it back as his ancestral land.

keyTerms.meaning: 'To the one from whom it was bought' – here, the כהן who sold the field
The buyer
The original owners of the family land

steps.whatToRemember: A field that went to the כהנים now counts as the כהן's land. At יובל it goes back to the כהן, not to the original family.

phrases.english: Then why does the verse say "to the one from whom it was bought"?
A field that went out to the priests,
and the priest sold it,
and the buyer consecrated it,
and someone else redeemed it:
one might think it returns to the original owners?
So the verse says "to the one from whom it was bought."
phrases.notes: That is the כהן who sold it to the buyer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: A field that went to the כהנים is treated as belonging to the כהן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The phrase לאשר קנהו in ויקרא 27:24 as explained by the ברייתא.

steps.title: Why the Torah needed both phrases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the Torah wrote both 'לא יגאל' and 'לאשר קנהו'. Without 'לאשר קנהו', we would not know the rule when the כהן sold the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah needed to write 'it shall not be redeemed,' and it also needed to write 'to the one from whom it was bought.' If the Torah had written only 'it shall not be redeemed,' we would apply it only where the field does not return at all. So the Torah also wrote 'to the one from whom it was bought.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the two phrases are not repeating each other. Each one teaches a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לא יגאל' teaches that the original owner loses the field. But it does not tell us what happens when the כהן sold the field and the buyer consecrated it. 'לאשר קנהו' is needed to teach that in that case it goes back to the כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed – used to show why two sources are both necessary
The Merciful One – a name for the Torah's Giver
'It shall not be redeemed' (ויקרא 27:20)

steps.whatToRemember: Both phrases are needed: 'לא יגאל' for the owner losing the field, and 'לאשר קנהו' for a field the כהן sold, which returns to the כהן.

phrases.english: And it was necessary to write "it shall not be redeemed,"
and it was necessary to write "to the one from whom it was bought,"
for if the Torah had written only "it shall not be redeemed,"
[we would say it applies where] it does not return at all,
phrases.notes: The גמרא doesn't spell out the whole thought here: from 'לא יגאל' alone, we wouldn't know about the case where the כהן sold the field.

phrases.english: so the Torah wrote "to the one from whom it was bought."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why both phrases from steps 7 and 9 are needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both לא יגאל and לאשר קנהו are necessary, since each covers a different case.

steps.title: Why the Torah also needed 'It shall not be redeemed'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its explanation from step 10. From לאשר קנהו alone, we could not have learned the case where the original owner pays to redeem the field. So the Torah also wrote לא יגאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the Torah had written only 'to the one who bought it,' we would say: that is where the owners paid nothing. But here the owners pay money, so maybe the field should stay with them. That is why the Torah wrote 'it shall not be redeemed.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of the 'why do we need both פסוקים' argument. Step 10 showed why לאשר קנהו is needed. Now the גמרא shows why לא יגאל is needed too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the לאשר קנהו case, a כהן sold the field and the buyer consecrated it, so the original owners paid nothing. In our case, a כהן consecrated it and the original owner paid הקדש to redeem it. Since he paid, we might think he gets his family field back for good, so the Torah needed לא יגאל to say it does not go back to him the old way.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Merciful One,' meaning the Torah
'To the one who bought it' (from the פסוק about a field returning at יובל)
'It shall not be redeemed' (from the פסוק about a consecrated field)
They give money (they pay)

phrases.english: And if the Torah had written only "to the one who bought it,"
[I would say that is because] the owners do not give any money,
but here, where the owners do give money,
[I would say] that it should stay in their hands,
so the Torah wrote "it shall not be redeemed."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the 'both are needed' argument that step 10 began
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לא יגאל is needed to teach that even when the original owner pays to redeem a field that a כהן consecrated, it does not go back to him as his family field.

steps.title: Why the Torah added the word 'anymore'
steps.stepSummary: Without the word עוד, we would think the owner can never redeem the field at all. עוד teaches that he cannot redeem it back to how it was before. He can still redeem it, but it becomes like a purchased field.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the Torah had written 'it shall not be redeemed' without 'anymore,' I would think it can never be redeemed. So the Torah wrote 'anymore': it cannot be redeemed back to the way it was, but it can be redeemed and held like a purchased field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the extra word עוד is needed. This supports the reading from step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לא יגאל by itself sounds like a total ban on redeeming. Adding עוד ('any more,' meaning 'again as before') narrows the ban. He cannot get the field back as a family inheritance, but he may redeem it as a שדה מקנה, a field that goes out of his hands at יובל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Anymore' (the extra word in the פסוק)
I would have thought (an idea that turns out to be wrong)
Back to the way it was before
A purchased field, which goes out of the buyer's hands at יובל

steps.whatToRemember: עוד means the owner can still redeem the field, but only as a purchased field, never again as his family inheritance.

phrases.english: And if the Torah had written "it shall not be redeemed"
and had not written "anymore,"
I would have said it cannot be redeemed at all.
So the Torah wrote "anymore,"
meaning: it cannot be redeemed back to the way it was,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל נִגְאֶלֶת שֶׁתְּהֵא לְפָנָיו כִּשְׂדֵה מִקְנָה.
phrases.english: but it can be redeemed so that he holds it like a purchased field.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״, וְלָא כְּתַב ״עוֹד״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the need for לא יגאל to the need for the extra word עוד, closing the answer to step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עוד limits לא יגאל: the owner may redeem the field, but only as a שדה מקנה.

steps.title: So what is the answer to our original question?
steps.stepSummary: The detour about עוד is finished. The גמרא now asks what the final answer is to the original question: when the owner redeems his field in the second יובל, does he count as 'another person'?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the conclusion about it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its earlier open question and asks for a final ruling. This line sets up the next step, where a source is brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof the גמרא tried from the ברייתא about עוד did not work, because every opinion needs עוד for its own lesson. So the גמרא needs a new source, and the next step brings one.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What came of it?' The final answer to an open question

phrases.english: What is the conclusion about it?
phrases.notes: 'It' is the earlier question: when the owner redeems in the second יובל, is he like 'another person'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 12 shows that עוד is needed by everyone, the גמרא returns to the open question
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether an owner who redeems his consecrated field in the second יובל is treated like 'another person,' so that the field goes to the כהנים at יובל

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the field goes to the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי אליעזר. If the owner redeems the field during the second יובל, the field goes to the כהנים at יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי אליעזר says, if the owners redeemed it in the second יובל, it goes out to the כהנים at יובל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא. רבי אליעזר rules that an owner who redeems in the second יובל does not keep the field. It goes to the כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This treats the owner in the second יובל just like an outsider who redeemed the field. In that case, too, the field goes to the כהנים at יובל. So the answer is that he is like 'another person.'

keyTerms.meaning: The second יובל cycle, after the first יובל has already passed
It goes out to the כהנים

phrases.english: Come and hear: רבי אליעזר says:
If the owners redeemed it in the second יובל,
it goes out to the כהנים at the יובל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to רבי אליעזר, an owner who redeems in the second יובל does not keep the field. It goes to the כהנים at יובל, so he is treated like another person.

steps.title: רבינא: but the משנה says 'until another redeems it'
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges רב אשי. In the משנה, רבי אליעזר says the כהנים only receive the field if 'another' person redeems it. That sounds like the owner is never counted as 'another.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: But we did not learn it that way! רבי אליעזר says: the כהנים do not enter the field until another person redeems it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא raises a contradiction between the ברייתא in step 14 and the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's word 'another' suggests that only an outsider's redemption sends the field to the כהנים. If so, when the owner himself redeems it, even in the second יובל, he should keep it. That clashes with the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But we did not learn it this way!' (pointing to a different wording in the משנה)
Another person, someone other than the owner
They enter into it, meaning they take ownership of the field

phrases.english: רבינא said to רב אשי:
But we did not learn it this way!

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אֵין הַכֹּהֲנִים נִכְנָסִין לְתוֹכָהּ
phrases.english: רבי אליעזר says: The כהנים do not take possession of it
until another person redeems it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 14 using the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that an owner who redeems in the second יובל loses the field to the כהנים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה makes the כהנים' ownership depend on 'another' redeeming. An owner is not 'another,' so his redemption should not send the field to the כהנים.

steps.title: In the second יובל, the owner counts as 'another'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that once we are in the second יובל, the owner is treated like 'another person.' So the משנה and the ברייתא agree.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The owners in the second יובל are considered like another person.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי settles the contradiction by explaining the word 'another' in the משנה. This also answers the question from step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Another' in the משנה does not only mean a stranger. It also includes the owner himself if he redeems after the first יובל has passed. Since he counts as 'another' then, the field goes to the כהנים, just as the ברייתא says.

keyTerms.meaning: They are like another person

steps.whatToRemember: In this first version: an owner who redeems his field during the second יובל is like 'another person,' so at יובל the field goes to the כהנים. The איכא דאמרי in steps 17-19 reaches the opposite result.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'another' in the משנה as only 'a stranger.' Here the owner himself counts as 'another' once the first יובל has passed.
steps.whyThisMatters: According to the first version, this answers the question from step 13 and shows that רבי אליעזר's משנה and ברייתא agree. The second version (steps 17-19) disagrees.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Owners in the second יובל are like another person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge in step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a term: 'another' in the משנה includes the owner in the second יובל
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Another' means only someone other than the owner, so the owner's redemption never sends the field to the כהנים
steps.terutzMaskana: An owner who redeems in the second יובל is counted as 'another,' so the field goes to the כהנים. The משנה and the ברייתא agree.

steps.title: Another version: the field stays with the owner
steps.stepSummary: A different version of the ברייתא has רבי אליעזר rule that if the owner redeems in the second יובל, the field does not go to the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the ברייתא reads differently: רבי אליעזר says that if the owner redeemed the field during the second יובל, it does not go to the כהנים at יובל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the ברייתא from Step 14, and it gives the opposite answer to the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, a field redeemed in the second יובל went to the כהנים. In this version it does not. That means the owner is not treated like 'another person,' even in the second יובל.

keyTerms.meaning: The second יובל cycle after the field was made הקדש
It does not go out to the כהנים

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is a different version of the same discussion from Steps 14–16, and it reaches the opposite result.

phrases.english: Some say:
phrases.notes: This starts a whole second version of the discussion from Steps 14–16.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
If he redeemed it in the second Jubilee,
it does not go out to the priests at the Jubilee.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the ברייתא of Step 14 with a version that gives the opposite ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the owner redeeming in the second יובל count as 'another person'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. The field does not go to the כהנים, so the owner is not like 'another person.'

steps.title: Why do we need the ברייתא if the משנה already says this?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the משנה already teaches that the כהנים only receive the field if someone else redeems it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: We already learn this in our משנה. רבי אליעזר says the כהנים do not enter the field unless another person redeems it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges the need for the ברייתא, since the משנה seems to teach the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the כהנים get the field only if 'another' person redeems it. That sounds like the owner never makes the field go to the כהנים. So why does the ברייתא need to say so?

keyTerms.meaning: We also learned this: the source already exists in the משנה
Another person, someone other than the owner
Enter into it: the כהנים take possession of the field

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
We also learn this [in the mishna]:
Rabbi Eliezer says:
The priests do not enter into it
until another person redeems it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the ברייתא in Step 17 is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the ברייתא in Step 17
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's word 'another' already shows that the owner does not cause the field to go to the כהנים, so the ברייתא seems to add nothing.

steps.title: From the משנה alone we might have thought the owner counts as 'another'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the משנה alone could suggest the owner counts as 'another' in the second יובל. The ברייתא teaches that he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: From the משנה alone, I would have said that in the second יובל the owner is like another person. The ברייתא teaches us that he is not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains why the ברייתא is still needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says 'another' person. Someone could think that by the second יובל, the owner is far enough removed to count as 'another.' The ברייתא rules this out: even then, the owner keeps the field.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought: the mistaken first assumption
It teaches us: the new point the source adds
The owner
Is considered like another person

steps.whatToRemember: In this second version, רבי אליעזר holds that the owner is never 'another person,' even in the second יובל. In the first version (Step 16), he is.

phrases.english: He said to him:
If from the mishna, I would have said:
the owner in the second Jubilee
is like another person;
it teaches us [otherwise].
phrases.notes: The ברייתא is what teaches us that the owner is not like another person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge from Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the ברייתא adds something the משנה leaves open
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In the second יובל, the owner counts as 'another person.'
steps.terutzMaskana: Even in the second יובל, the owner is not 'another,' and the field stays his.

steps.title: A son buys a field from his father: רבי מאיר's view
steps.stepSummary: If the father died before the son was מקדיש the field, it is a שדה אחוזה. If the father died after, it is a שדה מקנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone buys a field from his father. If the father dies and then the son is מקדיש it, it is like a שדה אחוזה. If the son is מקדיש it and then the father dies, it is like a שדה מקנה. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It discusses a field that was bought but would later have been inherited anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the father dies, the son inherits the family rights, so the field becomes his ancestral field. For רבי מאיר, what matters is the status at the moment of הקדש. If the father was still alive then, the field was only purchased.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
An ancestral, inherited family field
A purchased field, which returns to its family owner at יובל
He consecrated it to the Temple

steps.whyThisMatters: The two types of field have different redemption prices and different rules at יובל.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who buys a field from his father,
and his father died,
and afterward he consecrated it —
it is like an ancestral field.
If he consecrated it and afterward his father died —
it is like a purchased field;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the end of the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The field's status follows whether the father died before or after the הקדש.

steps.title: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון: it is always a שדה אחוזה
steps.stepSummary: They learn from the פסוק that a שדה מקנה means only a field that could never become ancestral. A field the son will inherit is not included.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון say it is like a שדה אחוזה. The פסוק says 'a field of his purchase, which is not of his ancestral field.' That means a field that cannot become ancestral. This field, which will become ancestral, is excluded.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון disagree with רבי מאיר and bring a פסוק as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'which is not of his ancestral field' limit the rules of a שדה מקנה to a field that will never be ancestral. This field is due to become ancestral when the father dies. So even if the son was מקדיש it while the father was alive, it is treated as a שדה אחוזה.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit or due to become
This case is excluded
As it is stated: introduces a פסוק

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon say:
it is like an ancestral field,
as it is stated:
"If ... a field of his purchase,
which is not of his ancestral field" —
a field that is not fit
to become an ancestral field;
this excludes this one, which is fit
to become an ancestral field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי מאיר's second case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A field that is due to become ancestral is treated as a שדה אחוזה, even if it was made הקדש before the father died.

steps.title: A purchased field never goes to the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: A שדה מקנה that was made הקדש does not go to the כהנים at יובל, because the buyer only owned it until יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: A שדה מקנה does not go to the כהנים at יובל, because a person cannot be מקדיש something that is not his.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a general rule about a purchased field at יובל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer's ownership only lasts until יובל, when the field returns to its family owner. Since the buyer never owned the field past יובל, his הקדש cannot hand it over to the כהנים forever.

keyTerms.term: אֵין אָדָם מַקְדִּישׁ דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: A person cannot consecrate what is not his

phrases.english: A purchased field does not go out
to the priests at the Jubilee,
because a person cannot consecrate
something that is not his.

steps.triggerLanguage: שדה מקנה אינה יוצאה לכהנים ביובל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a general rule about purchased fields.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A הקדש of a שדה מקנה does not pass to the כהנים at יובל.

steps.title: כהנים and לוים can always consecrate and redeem
steps.stepSummary: כהנים and לוים may be מקדיש and redeem their fields at any time, before or after יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The כהנים and the לוים may always be מקדיש their fields and may always redeem them, both before יובל and after יובל.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a special rule for כהנים and לוים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For כהנים and לוים, the usual time limits around יובל do not apply. They can always be מקדיש and always redeem.

keyTerms.meaning: Always, at any time
They redeem

steps.whatToRemember: A שדה מקנה never goes to the כהנים. כהנים and לוים may always be מקדיש and redeem.

phrases.english: The priests and the Levites may always consecrate,
and may always redeem,
both before the Jubilee
and after the Jubilee.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a special rule for כהנים and לוים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים and לוים may be מקדיש and redeem at any time, before or after יובל.

steps.title: Field bought from father, made הקדש before the father died
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: according to רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, if a son bought his father's field, was מקדיש it, and then the father died, it is treated as a שדה אחוזה. The reason is that the פסוק only calls a field שדה מקנה if it can never become ancestral.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא. The Sages taught: How do we know that if someone buys a field from his father, makes it הקדש, and then his father dies, it counts for him as an ancestral field? The פסוק says, "And if a field he bought, which is not of his ancestral field." That means a field that is not set to become ancestral. This field is excluded, because it is set to become ancestral. These are the words of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a ברייתא. In it, רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון teach that a field a son bought from his father counts as a שדה אחוזה, even if he was מקדיש it while his father was still alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key word is the פסוק's phrase "which is not of his ancestral field." רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון read it as "not even due to become ancestral." Since this field will come to the son through inheritance anyway, it already counts as ancestral at the time he was מקדיש it.

keyTerms.meaning: An ancestral field, one that came to a person through his family's inheritance
A purchased field, which goes back to the original family at יובל
He consecrated it, meaning he gave it to the Temple treasury
The פסוק teaches; this introduces the verse used as the source
Fit to become, or due to become, in the future

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the order of events. Here the son was מקדיש the field first, and only afterward did the father die. That is the opposite order from רבי מאיר's case in the next step.

phrases.english: GEMARA
The Sages taught:
From where do we know, for one who buys a field from his father
and consecrated it, and afterward his father died,
from where do we know that it is treated for him like an ancestral field?
The verse states:
"And if a field that he has bought
which is not of his ancestral field"

phrases.aramaic: שָׂדֶה שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לִהְיוֹת שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה,
phrases.english: meaning a field that is not due to become an ancestral field,

phrases.aramaic: יָצְתָה זוֹ, שֶׁרְאוּיָה לִהְיוֹת שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה,
phrases.english: which excludes this one, since it is due to become an ancestral field.
These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִנַּיִן לְלוֹקֵחַ שָׂדֶה מֵאָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא on the משנה's case of a field bought from the father, giving the ברייתא's source for it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, a field bought from the father and made הקדש before the father died is a שדה אחוזה, because it is due to become ancestral.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: only once the father has died
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר uses the same פסוק, but only for the case where the father died first and the son was מקדיש the field afterward. In his reading, the field must actually be ancestral at the time it is made הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: How do we know that if someone buys a field from his father, and the father dies, and only afterward he makes it הקדש, it counts as an ancestral field? The פסוק says, "And if a field he bought, which is not of his ancestral field." That means a field that is not ancestral. This field is excluded, because it already is ancestral.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר gives a different reading of the same פסוק. He applies it only where the father was already dead when the son was מקדיש the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר reads "not of his ancestral field" as "not ancestral right now," not as "not due to become ancestral." So in his view, a field that will only become ancestral later is still a שדה מקנה at the time it is made הקדש. Only once the father has died does it become a שדה אחוזה.

keyTerms.meaning: Which IS an ancestral field, already, at this moment
This one is excluded from the rule of a שדה מקנה

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree on the case where the father died first. They argue about the case where the son was מקדיש the field while the father was still alive: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון say it is ancestral, and רבי מאיר says it is purchased.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
From where do we know, for one who buys a field from his father,
and his father died, and afterward he consecrated it,
from where do we know that it is treated for him like an ancestral field?
The verse states:
"And if a field that he has bought
which is not of his ancestral field"
meaning a field that is not an ancestral field,
which excludes this one, since it is an ancestral field.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִן לְלוֹקֵחַ שָׂדֶה מֵאָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the ברייתא's מחלוקת, reading the same פסוק more narrowly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, the field counts as a שדה אחוזה only if the father died before the son was מקדיש it.

steps.title: Suggestion: the argument depends on קנין פירות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the two sides argue about whether owning only the right to a field's produce (קנין פירות) counts like owning the field itself (קנין הגוף).
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that this is what they argue about? רבי מאיר holds that owning the produce is like owning the field itself. רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון hold that owning the produce is not like owning the field itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes a deeper reason behind the מחלוקת. It ties the argument to a general question: is a buyer who has rights to a field's produce considered a full owner of the field?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A buyer of a field only keeps it until יובל, so what he really has is rights to the produce. רבי מאיר holds this counts like full ownership, so the son already fully owned the field and the father's death changes nothing on its own. That is why he needs the פסוק for the case where the father has died. רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון hold that the son only gets the field itself at the father's death, which obviously makes it ancestral, so they use the פסוק for the earlier case instead.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? This introduces a suggestion the גמרא is testing
They argue, or they disagree
Ownership of the produce, the right to use the field and its crops
Ownership of the actual field itself
Is equal to, or is considered like

steps.confusionAlert: "לימא" is only a suggestion. The גמרא often goes on to reject a לימא, so do not treat it as the final explanation yet.
steps.whyThisMatters: Whether קנין פירות counts like קנין הגוף is a major question that comes up all over ש״ס. Here the גמרא is testing whether this מחלוקת depends on it.

phrases.english: Shall we say that they disagree about this:
that Rabbi Meir holds:
ownership of the produce is like ownership of the field itself.
phrases.notes: A buyer only keeps the field until יובל, so he really owns just its produce.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon hold:

phrases.aramaic: קִנְיַן פֵּירוֹת לָאו כְּקִנְיַן הַגּוּף דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: ownership of the produce is not like ownership of the field itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the underlying principle behind the two readings of the פסוק in steps 24 and 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Suggested: רבי מאיר holds קנין פירות is like קנין הגוף, and רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון hold it is not.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: In general, they hold קנין פירות is like קנין הגוף
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק begins answering the suggestion from Step 26. He says that in general, רבי שמעון and רבי יהודה hold that owning a field's produce counts like owning the field itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: In general, according to רבי שמעון and רבי יהודה, owning the right to an item's produce is considered like owning the item itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק starts to answer the suggestion that the whole argument is about קנין פירות. He first states their general position, and this sets up the rest of his explanation, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בְּעָלְמָא, 'in general', signals that he is describing their usual view on קנין פירות, not yet explaining this specific case. By stating their general view first, he is preparing to show why that idea alone does not fully explain their ruling about the son's field. The full reasoning continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: In general; in other cases (not just this one)
Owning only the right to an item's produce or use
Owning the item itself
Is similar to; is treated like

steps.confusionAlert: This line is only the opening of רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer. Do not treat it as his full answer. He has stated their general view, and his explanation of this case comes next.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
In general, according to Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Yehuda,
owning the produce is like owning the item itself,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: בְּעָלְמָא לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to Step 26's suggestion that the argument depends on קנין פירות, starting by stating רבי שמעון and רבי יהודה's general position.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה / רבי שמעון is simply about קנין פירות.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: He begins by stating that רבי שמעון and רבי יהודה generally hold קנין פירות is like קנין הגוף. His explanation of how this affects the suggestion continues in the next lines.
